speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the exact nature of the pain—does it feel sharp, burning, or like an electric shock—and on which side of your body is it occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sharp, radiating pain suggests possible nerve involvement, so I need to check for neurological deficits. Do you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your foot or toes, and can you stand on your tiptoes and heels on the affected side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness in the saddle area, and have you noticed any swelling or bruising in your lower back or leg?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. To narrow down the specific nerve root involved, can you tell me exactly where in your leg the numbness or pain is most intense—is it the outer calf and little toe, or the top of the foot and big toe? Additionally, does bending forward or sitting relieve the pain, or does it make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, the absence of red flag symptoms like fever or incontinence helps rule out more serious conditions like infection or cauda equina syndrome. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to visualize the spine; REQUEST TEST: MRI_Lumbar_Spine.
